content:
The number \(17017\) factors into primes as \(17017 = 7 \times 11 \times 13 \times 17\). Therefore,
\[
17017^{17} = 7^{17} \times 11^{17} \times 13^{17} \times 17^{17}.
\]
Any positive divisor \(d\) has the form \(d = 7^a \times 11^b \times 13^c \times 17^d\) with \(0 \le a,b,c,d \le 17\). We need \(d \equiv 5 \pmod{12}\).

Reduce the bases modulo 12:
\[
7 \equiv 7,\quad 11 \equiv 11 \equiv -1,\quad 13 \equiv 1,\quad 17 \equiv 5.
\]
Their powers modulo 12 are:
\[
7^a \equiv \begin{cases} 1 & a \text{ even} \\ 7 & a \text{ odd} \end{cases},\qquad
11^b \equiv \begin{cases} 1 & b \text{ even} \\ 11 & b \text{ odd} \end{cases},
\]
\[
13^c \equiv 1 \text{ always},\qquad
17^d \equiv 5^d \equiv \begin{cases} 1 & d \text{ even} \\ 5 & d \text{ odd} \end{cases}.
\]
Thus the condition reduces to
\[
7^a \cdot 11^b \cdot 17^d \equiv 5 \pmod{12}.
\]
Testing the eight parity combinations for \((a,b,d)\):
- (even, even, odd): \(1 \cdot 1 \cdot 5 = 5 \equiv 5\) ✓
- (odd, odd, even): \(7 \cdot 11 \cdot 1 = 77 \equiv 5\) ✓
All other combinations yield \(1,7,\) or \(11 \not\equiv 5\).

The ranges \(0 \le a,b,c,d \le 17\) contain \(18\) integers each. Among these, there are \(9\) even numbers (\(0,2,\dots,16\)) and \(9\) odd numbers (\(1,3,\dots,17\)). The exponent \(c\) can be any of the \(18\) values.

Counting the valid choices:
- Case 1 (even \(a\), even \(b\), odd \(d\)): \(9 \times 9 \times 9 \times 18\)
- Case 2 (odd \(a\), odd \(b\), even \(d\)): \(9 \times 9 \times 9 \times 18\)

These are disjoint, so the total number \(N\) is
\[
N = 2 \cdot 9^3 \cdot 18 = 2 \cdot 729 \cdot 18 = 26244.
\]
The remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(1000\) is \(26244 \bmod 1000 = 244\).

\boxed{244}
